To define $ \Delta S_{conf} $ we begin by comparing the adsorption of alkanes in five different zeolite structures: MFI, CHA, TON, FAU, and MOR. Depicted in Figure 2A is the relationship between the entropy of an adsorbed molecule (alkanes and permanent gases) and its gas-phase entropy, where the molecular entropy on the surface never exceeds that in the gas phase. While a significant loss in entropy occurs in all five zeolites, the absolute loss in entropy is distinct for each framework. Adsorbates in TON exhibit the largest loss in entropy upon adsorption, while FAU results in the smallest entropic losses. If the molecules were to behave as immobile adsorbates on the surface, the entropy lost upon adsorption ( $ \Delta S_{ads} $) can be approximated to be equal to three degrees of translational freedom, $ ^{3,35,36} $ which can be calculated from statistical mechanics using the Sackur–Tetrode equation $ ^{37} $

ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

On the basis of this shape-selective feature , highly effective molecular separations and selective catalytic conversions can be achieved within zeolitic structures that are difficult to accomplish with other materials and/or techniques . $ ^ { 1-3 } $ So far, several shape-selectivity mechanisms have been elucidated and applications identified. $ ^{2-18} $ In common molecular sieving, bulky molecules adsorb preferentially over bulkier species as a result of steric constraints imposed by the zeolites' framework, e.g., linear alkane molecules compared to branched isomers. $ ^{19-23} $ Besides this common adsorption competition based on molecular bulkiness, the reverse phenomenon can also occur, i.e., competitive adsorption in favor of the bulkier species. Experiments revealed preferential adsorption of branched alkanes over their linear isomers on specific zeolites with tubular pore systems such as SAPO-5 and Mordenite. $ ^{24-28} $ Molecular simulations indicated that in such zeolites, depending on conditions, branched alkanes are preferentially adsorbed at the expense of linear isomers. $ ^{29-34} $ The present manuscript discusses the mechanisms of shape selectivity in n- and isoalkane adsorption on zeolite MCM-22. This zeolite with IZA code MWW is a relatively new synthetic material that has an unusual and quite complex pore structure. $ ^{35} $ Its framework is composed of two independent pore systems. The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The corresponding calculated entropies (S) includes translational, ( $ S_{t} $) vibrational, ( $ S_{v} $) and rotational ( $ S_{r} $) degrees of freedom: $ S = S_{t} + S_{v} + S_{r} $. All the considered systems are in singlet state, thus the electronic contribution to the entropy is zero. Since both adsorbed molecules are constrained in the zeolite cavity their entropy contributions in the adsorption complexes were corrected as follows: the translational and rotational degrees of freedom were reduced by 1 and 1.28 [37]. The Gibbs free energies of the zeolite support consist of only vibrational and electronic contributions. The expressions of all enthalpy and entropy contributions can be found in Ref. [38].

The first attempts to describe guest-induced flexibility in zeolites were done using molecular dynamics simulations. $ ^{79-82} $ Rigid zeolitic force fields were dynamically modified using transition state theory to include lattice flexibility, and the results obtained by these models were in good agreement with experimental data. $ ^{79-81,83,84} $ It was shown that framework flexibility in silicalite-1 (MFI-type framework) is responsible for the adsorption of large molecules such as isobutane and heptane with inflection behavior at high loadings, $ ^{80} $ while enhanced self-diffusivity at low loadings of short alkanes (i.e. methane and n-butane) was observed. $ ^{81} $ Framework flexibility is also crucial for aromatics adsorption on MFI zeolite, especially at high pressures. $ ^{84,85} $ While the use of rigid zeolitic models led to the underestimation of the aromatics adsorption in MFI zeolite by a factor of two, $ ^{84,85} $ the use of flexible models to simulate diffusion coefficients of various alkanes in silicalite-1 zeolite resulted in a convergence of experimental and theoretical values. $ ^{86} $ Recently by using in situ integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC-STEM) while adsorbing benzene molecules on MFI zeolite, Xiong et al. showed that the MFI structure goes through severe deformations giving another proof of guest-induced flexibility in zeolites (see Fig. 4). $ ^{87} $

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

The turnover rates of olefin formation during cyclohexanol (CyOH) dehydration within the autoclave reactor initially increase with the local ionic strength within a micropore, and further decrease along ionic strength promotion, shown as a volcano-shaped dependence of TOFs on the ionic strength of zeolites. The local ionic environments with moderate-to-high ionic strength alter the adsorption of uncharged reactants, and stabilize surface intermediates and positively charge the transition states, which eventually increase the reaction rates. But the formation and size of the H₃O⁺(H₂O)ₙ₋₁ in the zeolite pores limit the adsorption of CyOH, e.g., size exclusion effects, and decrease reaction rates. On the other hand, the higher ionic strength results in increased excess chemical potentials of the charged transition states, which in turn raises the activation Gibbs free energies²¹⁻²⁵. In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via

$$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$

$$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$

where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as

$$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$

where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows.

descriptor_candidates.name: occupiable_volume_entropy_loss
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H1 (mechanism: confinement in occupiable free volume freezes translational freedom; loss of entropy scales inversely with accessible pore volume per gram and per molecule). Regime: pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, small-to-medium adsorbates. Falsification: if a descriptor built from AV and Vol fails to reduce MAE of entropy loss/R versus a 14-input neural network baseline by more than the reported seed variance, the dominant-volume mechanism is falsified for this dataset.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Known statistical-mechanics picture (Sackur-Tetrode translational loss; E01, E02): smaller occupiable volume constrains the configurational integral, raising |Δs_ads|. Inference: geometric free-volume terms AV (m^2/g-scale source value, unverified units) and Vol jointly encode pore and molecule volume; their geometric mean is a single confinement index. This is a re-expression of E02's single-descriptor claim, so classified known_relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: MAE(descriptor alone or as added feature) >= MAE(14-input baseline) within seed uncertainty; or residuals correlate with a non-volume descriptor (e.g., PBF) stronger than with AV, indicating confinement geometry, not volume, controls entropy loss.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_mismatch_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H2 (mechanism: entropy loss grows with the mismatch between molecular anisotropy/asphericity and pore-window geometry; near-spherical or compact molecules retain rotational freedom in cylindrical channels, while elongated/flat molecules lose both translational and rotational entropy when span exceeds the largest free-sphere diameter). Regime: molecular sieving regime where molecule size is comparable to pore diameter (0.4–0.8 nm windows). Falsification: if multiplying molecular shape ratios (PBF/SPAN, PMI anisotropy) by the pore-diameter ratio (lsd_p/lsd_f) does not improve MAE of entropy loss/R over a volume-only descriptor, shape matching is not the operative mechanism here.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01/E04/E07 show confinement entropy depends on molecular shape vs pore geometry, not volume alone; E10 notes molecules can squeeze into pores smaller than their size. Inference: combining principal-moment anisotropy (PMI2/PMI3), PBF/SPAN asphericity, and the lsd_p/lsd_f window-to-pore ratio yields a dimensionless fit-mismatch index. Distinct from H1 because it is volume-independent. This combination is new, hence new_combination.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: MAE of a model using only H2's descriptor exceeds MAE of the volume-only descriptor H1, or the log-anisotropy term's coefficient is statistically indistinguishable from zero across CV folds.

descriptor_candidates.name: framework_rigidity_cage_index
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(AV * density / ASA) - log(abs(PBF)) ** 2 + maximum(lsd_f, lsd_p) / minimum(lsd_f, lsd_p)
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H3 (mechanism: adsorption entropy loss depends on the cage/channel character of the framework, not just pore size; dense, small-pore frameworks (high ASA per pore volume, high source-scale density) act as rigid cages that freeze rotations and translations, while large-cavity frameworks (FAU-like) permit residual rotational entropy). Regime: comparison across framework topologies at 298 K, infinite dilution. Falsification: if the ASA/(AV·density)-type rigidity-cage term plus the lsd ratio does not lower MAE of entropy loss/R relative to a pure size descriptor, cage character contributes no information beyond pore volume.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 (framework-dependent entropy loss: TON largest, FAU smallest), E05 (rotational degrees of freedom reduced by confinement factors), E06 (framework flexibility/rigidity modulates adsorbed states). Inference: ASA per occupiable volume indexes the fraction of framework surface confining the guest; the max/min lsd ratio separates single-channel (ratio≈1) from cage-with-window (ratio≫1) topologies. Distinct from H1 and H2 because it targets framework rigidity/topology. New combination of existing inputs.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Adding H3's descriptor to the 14-input network does not reduce MAE of entropy loss/R beyond seed noise; or within the TON/FAU contrast of E01 the descriptor ordering fails (TON not ranked above FAU in predicted entropy loss).

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_confinement_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H1 (mechanism: entropy loss is governed by the density of confining surface per occupiable pore volume, plus the per-molecule volume share; frameworks with high accessible surface area relative to their occupiable volume freeze more guest degrees of freedom, and heavier/larger molecules in a fixed pore volume lose proportionally more translational entropy per Sackur-Tetrode-like scaling). Regime: pure-silica zeolites, infinite dilution, 298 K, small-to-medium adsorbates. Falsification: if the ASA/AV surface-density term combined with the per-mass molecular volume term does not reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below the retained volume-only descriptor (MAE_R = 0.5634) beyond seed variance, surface confinement contributes nothing beyond occupiable volume.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01/E02: entropy loss varies by framework and correlates with occupiable volume; E09 derives entropy loss from the configurational partition function, which is reduced by the accessible surface that constrains configurations. Inference: ASA per unit occupiable volume indexes how strongly the framework surface packs around the guest; Vol/(MW+1) is a molecule-volume-per-mass proxy for the translational configurational integral. Distinct from the retained H1 because it encodes surface-to-volume ratio, not volume alone. Re-expression of known confinement physics using fixed inputs, hence known_relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: MAE of entropy loss/R with this descriptor added to (or replacing part of) the 14-input baseline fails to improve by more than the reported seed variance, or residuals anti-correlate with the descriptor (more confining surface predicts less entropy loss).

descriptor_candidates.name: anisotropy_rotational_freeze
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H2 (mechanism: rotational entropy loss upon confinement depends on molecular anisotropy, independent of pore volume; near-spherical molecules (PMI1≈PMI2≈PMI3) retain rotation in cages, while elongated or flat molecules (large PMI ratios, large SPAN, small PBF) lose rotational freedom even in large pores). Regime: molecular-sieving regime where molecular dimension is comparable to window diameter (0.4-0.8 nm). Falsification: if a purely molecular-anisotropy descriptor, containing no framework descriptors, fails to improve MAE of entropy loss/R over the volume-only baseline, rotational freezing by shape mismatch is not an operative, additively recoverable mechanism in this dataset.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 (shape-confinement relation explicitly 'remains to be determined', translational+rotational losses reported separately), E07 (molecular symmetry strongly alters confined dynamics/rotation), E05 (rotational degrees of freedom reduced by confinement factors). Inference: principal-moment ratios are dimensionless anisotropy indices; SPAN and PBF capture asphericity. All terms are guarded with +1 or abs to avoid nonfinite values (previous round's shape descriptor failed on nonfinite values due to unguarded ratios). Volume-free descriptor, distinct from H1 and the prior rejected shape descriptor which mixed framework terms. New combination of existing inputs.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Descriptor-only or added-feature MAE of entropy loss/R exceeds the volume-only descriptor MAE (0.5634), or the anisotropy coefficient is statistically indistinguishable from zero across CV seeds.

candidates.hypothesis: H2 (mechanism: rotational entropy loss upon confinement depends on molecular anisotropy, independent of pore volume; near-spherical molecules (PMI1≈PMI2≈PMI3) retain rotation in cages, while elongated or flat molecules (large PMI ratios, large SPAN, small PBF) lose rotational freedom even in large pores). Regime: molecular-sieving regime where molecular dimension is comparable to window diameter (0.4-0.8 nm). Falsification: if a purely molecular-anisotropy descriptor, containing no framework descriptors, fails to improve MAE of entropy loss/R over the volume-only baseline, rotational freezing by shape mismatch is not an operative, additively recoverable mechanism in this dataset.
candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 (shape-confinement relation explicitly 'remains to be determined', translational+rotational losses reported separately), E07 (molecular symmetry strongly alters confined dynamics/rotation), E05 (rotational degrees of freedom reduced by confinement factors). Inference: principal-moment ratios are dimensionless anisotropy indices; SPAN and PBF capture asphericity. All terms are guarded with +1 or abs to avoid nonfinite values (previous round's shape descriptor failed on nonfinite values due to unguarded ratios). Volume-free descriptor, distinct from H1 and the prior rejected shape descriptor which mixed framework terms. New combination of existing inputs.
candidates.falsification_criteria: Descriptor-only or added-feature MAE of entropy loss/R exceeds the volume-only descriptor MAE (0.5634), or the anisotropy coefficient is statistically indistinguishable from zero across CV seeds.

candidates.name: window_cage_topology_index
candidates.formula: log(1 + maximum(lsd_f, lsd_p) / (minimum(lsd_f, lsd_p) + 0.1)) - log(1 + density) * (LabuteASA / (ASA + 1)) + log(1 + AV * density / (Vol + 1))
candidates.hypothesis: H3 (mechanism: entropy loss depends on framework topology class — cage-with-narrow-window frameworks (large disparity between largest and smallest limiting diameter, and high surface roughness per nominal area) act as rigid traps that freeze both translation and rotation, whereas one-dimensional large-channel frameworks permit residual freedom; density on its native numerical scale modulates the tightness of confinement). Regime: cross-topology comparison of pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, 298 K. Falsification: if the lsd-disparity topology term does not rank known contrast cases correctly (e.g., TON-type one-channel frameworks should show larger entropy loss than FAU-type large-cage frameworks per E01), or fails to reduce MAE of entropy loss/R beyond seed variance, cage/window topology carries no information beyond pore volume and molecular size.
candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 (TON largest, FAU smallest entropy loss across frameworks), E06 (framework rigidity/flexibility modulates adsorbed states), E10 (molecules can penetrate windows smaller than their size, implying window constraints are the active bottleneck). Inference: the max/min ratio of the two limiting diameters separates single-channel from cage-window topologies; LabuteASA/ASA (both positive, guarded) indexes surface granularity; AV*density/Vol is a dimensionally mixed but purely numerical packing index using density's native scale without assigning units. All divisions guarded by +1 or +0.1 constants to guarantee finiteness. New combination distinct from the prior rejected cage index (which used unguarded log(abs(PBF))**2 and caused nonfinite values).
candidates.falsification_criteria: Descriptor fails to reduce MAE of entropy loss/R versus the 14-input baseline beyond seed noise, or the predicted ordering of E01's framework contrast (TON > MFI/MOR > CHA > FAU in entropy loss) is not reproduced by descriptor rank.

rounds.retained_formula: log(1 + maximum(lsd_f, lsd_p) / (minimum(lsd_f, lsd_p) + 0.1)) - log(1 + density) * (LabuteASA / (ASA + 1)) + log(1 + AV * density / (Vol + 1))

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_per_volume_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H1' (mechanism: entropy loss scales with the confining surface area presented per unit of occupiable free volume, modulated by how tightly the molecule's own dimension fits inside the largest limiting diameter; high surface-to-volume frameworks confine guest configurations more strongly, raising |Δs_ads|/R, while a molecule whose cubic dimension approaches lsd_f has fewer accessible configurations). Regime: pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, 298 K, small-to-medium adsorbates. Falsification: if this surface-per-volume descriptor fails to beat the retained volume-only descriptor (MAE_R = 0.5634) by more than seed variance, surface confinement adds nothing beyond occupiable volume.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01/E02 establish that occupiable volume alone predicts entropy loss, and E09 shows entropy loss comes from reduction of the configurational partition function, which is bounded by the framework surface. Inference: ASA/AV indexes surface packing density around the guest; sqrt(Vol)/lsd_f is a dimensionless fit index. Re-expression of established confinement physics using fixed inputs, hence known_relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: MAE of entropy loss/R with this descriptor >= MAE of the retained volume-only descriptor (0.5634) within reported seed variance, or residuals correlate more strongly with a topology descriptor than with this one.

descriptor_candidates.name: squeeze_compliance_index
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + maximum(SPAN, sqrt(Vol)) / (lsd_p + 0.1)) + log(1 + MW / (AV * density + 1))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H4 (mechanism: entropy loss spikes when the molecule must distort to pass through or reside in windows smaller than its gas-phase size; E10 reports molecules can compress to ~80% of free size, and this forced deformation removes configurational microstates beyond what pore volume alone predicts, so entropy loss should grow with the ratio of molecular dimension to the smaller limiting diameter, weighted by molecular mass as a deformability/inertia proxy at fixed pore loading). Regime: molecular-sieving regime where molecular dimension is comparable to or exceeds window diameter (roughly lsd_p in 0.4-0.8 nm). Falsification: if the squeeze-ratio term does not improve MAE of entropy loss/R over the retained H1 and H3 descriptors beyond seed variance, window-size squeeze contributes no information beyond volume and topology.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E10 (molecules penetrate pores up to ~20% smaller than their free size, implying deformation-induced entropy loss), E01 (molecular shape vs confinement relation explicitly undetermined). Inference: maximum(SPAN, sqrt(Vol)) is a molecular largest-dimension proxy; its ratio to lsd_p measures squeeze severity; MW/(AV·density) is a guarded mass-per-occupiable-volume index on density's native numerical scale. Distinct from retained descriptors because it is a molecule-window mismatch term, not volume or topology disparity alone.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Adding this descriptor to the 14-input network fails to reduce MAE of entropy loss/R beyond seed noise, or predicted entropy loss does not increase for pairs where SPAN > lsd_p relative to SPAN << lsd_p pairs.

descriptor_candidates.name: mobility_trap_asymmetry_index
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + abs(PMI1 - PMI3) / (abs(PMI3) + 1) * maximum(lsd_f, lsd_p) / (minimum(lsd_f, lsd_p) + 0.1)) + 0.25 * log(1 + LabuteASA / (Vol + 1) * AV)
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: H5 (mechanism: entropy loss is maximal where anisotropic molecules meet cage-window topologies: elongated/flat molecules (large PMI1-PMI3 disparity) lose both rotational and translational freedom when trapped between narrow windows (large lsd disparity), whereas such molecules retain residual rotation in one-dimensional channels; the surface-granularity term LabuteASA·AV/Vol indexes how much irregular accessible surface further restricts orientational microstates). Regime: cross-topology, cross-adsorbate comparison of pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, 298 K. Falsification: if the anisotropy×topology interaction does not reduce MAE of entropy loss/R beyond seed variance, or if the interaction term does not discriminate E01's contrast set (elongated alkanes in TON should show the largest loss), the coupled shape-topology mechanism is not operative and entropy loss factorizes into independent molecule and framework terms.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence E01 (shape-confinement relation undetermined; TON largest, FAU smallest entropy loss), E07 (molecular symmetry strongly alters rotational/translational dynamics under confinement), E06 (framework rigidity modulates adsorbed states). Inference: the product of a guarded molecular anisotropy index and the retained topology-disparity ratio captures a coupling mechanism that neither term alone encodes; previous failures came from unguarded ratios, so all divisions here carry +1 or +0.1 guards and abs() on PMI differences. Distinct from H1 (volume), H3 (topology alone), H4 (size squeeze) because it is an anisotropy-topology interaction.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Descriptor fails to beat MAE_R = 0.5588 (best retained) beyond seed variance, or the predicted ordering within E01's framework contrast (TON > MFI/MOR > CHA > FAU entropy loss for elongated alkanes) is not reproduced by the descriptor's ranking.

retained.name: occupiable_volume_entropy_loss
retained.hypothesis: H1 (mechanism: confinement in occupiable free volume freezes translational freedom; loss of entropy scales inversely with accessible pore volume per gram and per molecule). Regime: pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, small-to-medium adsorbates. Falsification: if a descriptor built from AV and Vol fails to reduce MAE of entropy loss/R versus a 14-input neural network baseline by more than the reported seed variance, the dominant-volume mechanism is falsified for this dataset.
